dimension_justifications.soundness: Everything the paper literally states is carefully bounded, and every internal arithmetic relation I checked is exactly self-consistent (136.235/9.661 = 14.10x; 136.235/34.683 = 3.93x; 1 - 9.661/136.235 = 92.91%; 140.34 -> 15.89/10.01/9.74/8.41 = 88.68/92.87/93.06/94.01%; 1 - 2.229/4.901 = 54.5%; 139.53/15.89 = 8.78x and 324.09/15.89 = 20.39x; 209,920 = 20,992x10 and 635,520 = 20,992x30 + 192x30; 144 = 8x3x6, 12,960 = 8x3x540, 3,840 = 8x60x8, 540 = (1+8)x60). But three substantive gaps materially reduce confidence in the central quantitative claims. (1) 'Store' is the paper's headline estimand and is computed two different ways that are never reconciled: component accounting gives 136.235 and 9.661 MiB/doc (Table 1, Sec. 5.1, p.6) while a byte-range union gives 140.34 and 10.01 MiB/doc (Table 2, p.7) for the same stack, same frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy, and a strict item subset. (2) The model geometry needed to instantiate Eq. 2 (hidden size, KV heads, head dim, GDN convolution/recurrent shapes) is never given, so no reader can derive or sanity-check any Store number, and the per-layer policy's 'Q16 projections' component (Sec. 4.2 p.4, Tables 2 and 18) has no term in Eq. 2 at all. (3) The motivating budget of Eq. 1 (Sec. 3, p.3) is never tested: no experiment varies the hot-document set |H| or measures resident capacity, and Sec. 5.6 concedes that reducing Store 'does not by itself prove lower peak VRAM or serving capacity'. In addition, the 'no-cache dense recompute' baseline is undefined and its Table 2 numbers (TTFT 0.649 s, TPOT 648.75 ms) imply per-token full-prefix recomputation, and that baseline anchors the registered catastrophic-regression rule. This is 'plausible core with substantive gaps', not 'sound with minor gaps'.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The main narrative is genuinely well built: Sec. 3 fixes the target term before the method, Sec. 5.2/5.3/5.4 separate memory, latency, and quality instead of blending them, Figures 1 and 2 are legible and carry accurate scope banners ('Packed scope: retained per-document tensor state only'), blank TTFT/Recall cells are used deliberately with an explicit 'blank means unmeasured, not zero' convention, and the abstract itself names the adverse TTFT trade-off. Localized problems keep it from 4: Sec. 5.5 (pp.7-8) is three paragraphs of unexplained large counts (209,920; 635,520; 12,960; 96,660; 1,367-node tree) that a reader cannot evaluate; load-bearing verdict vocabulary ('scientifically valid', 'terminally complete', 'operationally invalid', 'raw-first', 'manifest-first') is never defined; 'projections' is used in three places with no definition; the split depth j = 7 used by every reported cohort appears only inside Figure 2 and never in prose; the decoding rule for the headline Table 1 is missing; and Sec. 5.5's 'stronger same-run hook' contradicts Appendix A's 'separate live-binding rerun binds a different frozen archive' (p.12).
dimension_justifications.contribution: The split-replay primitive is explicitly not claimed as new (Sec. 2, Table 11: 'we do not claim that primitive as new'), and the quantizer of Eq. 3 is textbook asymmetric groupwise min/max packing with BF16 scale/bias. What is genuinely new is (a) the accounting insight that a hybrid split-replay entry must count lower KV and convolution/recurrent state, not just the residual, and (b) the ForkAudit ownership-trace methodology. (a) is a real but modest framing contribution whose payoff is demonstrated only as a proxy metric on 60 items, two datasets, one model, one hardware family, one split depth, no Recall, and with an explicit disclaimer that it implies nothing about VRAM or capacity. (b) is substantial engineering, but the paper positions it as a complement rather than the contribution, its headline evidence is one historical defect plus constructed positive controls (which the paper correctly refuses to turn into a rate), and it is not packaged as something another group could apply to their own system. Net: narrow and of uncertain significance.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem split replay to memory-constrained hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLMs. An offline Write runs a document through split depth j = 7 and groupwise-packs the complete retained entry - boundary residual, lower full-attention KV, and lower convolution/recurrent state - at Q4/Q4/Q8 with BF16 scale/bias per 64-value group. An online Read dequantizes to BF16, shares immutable document tensors, creates request-private state via copy-on-write and recurrent rebinding, replays the query through the lower layers, and reconstructs the suffix. A fail-closed ForkAudit trace with seven targets validates the ownership boundary with phase-indexed storage evidence rather than output equality. Evidence: (i) an archival 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA validation cohort (Table 1) where the frozen policy cuts retained payload from 136.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (14.10x) at a paired mean-F1 difference of -0.39 points, 95% bootstrap [-2.04, 1.08]; (ii) a separate eight-item timing execution on the indices-6-9 subset (Table 2) showing the cost: TTFT 0.673 s versus 0.163 s for exact prefix caching and 7.15-7.19 versus 13.38 generated tokens/s, with TPOT within 2.5%; (iii) an ownership factorial (96 configurations, 8xH20-3e) where shared-document KV cuts the post-priming allocator delta from 4.901 to 2.229 GiB at N = 32 and a historical alias that output equality misses is exposed. The paper explicitly declines to claim lower total memory, Recall, edge performance, TTFT speedup, or broad quality preservation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The complete-entry capacity accounting. Counting only the depth-j residual understates a hybrid entry, and packing the whole entry composes two independent reductions - splitting (136.235 -> 34.683 MiB/doc, 3.93x) and quantization (34.683 -> 9.661 MiB/doc, giving 14.10x overall) - at a measured paired mean-F1 change of -0.39 points [-2.04, 1.08] with 0/60 items crossing the registered catastrophic threshold. I verified every one of these values, digit for digit, against claim_evidence_map.tsv rows C-QCOMEM-60-Q16-SPLIT-01 (34.683105 / 136.235352 / 3.9280x / 0.546238 / 0.542888), C-QCOMEM-60-STORE-F1-01 (9.660873 / 14.1018x / 0.542368 / -0.003870 / [-0.020365, 0.010756] / zero deltas <= -0.5) and C-QCOMEM-60-POLICY-TRADEOFF-01 (2.7495% / 7.536057 / 18.0778x / -0.054376 / [-0.115615, -0.001713] / five of 60). The paired discipline behind this cohort is also real: policies were calibrated on four disjoint prompts (indices 4-5 per dataset) that precede and do not overlap the validation indices 6-35.
strengths: The archival-cohort limitation is disclosed correctly and consistently, and I found no place where the paper describes it in stronger terms than the admission allows. The word 'archival' appears in the abstract (p.1), the contribution bullet (p.2), Sec. 5.1 ('archival, raw-first validation run'), Sec. 5.2, Sec. 5.6, the Conclusion, and Appendix H. Sec. 5.6 (p.9) states plainly that 'the original launcher used a mutable code directory and retained neither a pre-run full-source ledger nor a full model-weight ledger. We therefore do not describe it as fresh source-frozen regeneration.' Appendix A repeats it ('offline outcome replay therefore does not imply source-frozen GPU regeneration'), and Table 5's H20 archival row lists 'not source-frozen regeneration' in its exclusion column. The Reproducibility Statement uses the verb 'rechecks', which is outcome replay and not regeneration. This is exactly the right handling.

The trusted-computing-base exclusions are honest and, as far as I can check, never exceeded. Sec. 4.4 (p.5) names the TCB (capture/replay, mandatory-slot schema, slot-to-live-tensor binding, framework storage semantics) and states 'This is an offline, non-adversarial regression contract, not security attestation', excluding coherent omission/fabrication, transient writes between observations, compiled GDN, ATen/CUDA, and device/driver execution. Sec. 5.5's target-5 paragraph restates that the 209,920 + 635,520 receipts 'establish host-side selected launch/configuration provenance only, not device-side operator identity, execution, or completion'. Sec. 5.5 even self-limits its own null result: 'zero selected-context overlaps means only that this context never entered an allocator cell, not that the wrapper was absent or perturbation-free'. Table 5's exclusion column and Table 6's boundary column carry the same discipline per cohort.

Memory denominators are separated rather than conflated. Sec. 5.1's 'Memory denominators' paragraph explicitly distinguishes logical state, pages, synchronized allocator bytes, and unmeasured service capacity, and states that the Sec. 5.5 allocator result 'uses a third, distinct denominator'. Sec. 5.6 adds that the 14.10x and the 54.5% 'are not additive or interchangeable'. Most systems papers merge these.

Negative and adverse results are reported in the paper's own headline framing rather than buried. The abstract states that full-prefix Q16 is faster in TTFT (0.163 vs ~0.673 s) and higher in throughput (13.38 vs 7.15-7.19 tok/s) and concludes 'the supported contribution is capacity reduction with an explicit online cost, not TTFT acceleration'. Sec. 5.4 reports both mixed policies as ablations that lose, including the aggressive point whose interval lies below zero with 5/60 catastrophic items.

Blank cells are used as first-class evidence about what was not measured. Table 1's caption states 'Blank TTFT and Recall cells denote unmeasured metrics, not zeros', and Recall is disclaimed in the abstract, Sec. 5.1, Sec. 5.3, Sec. 5.4, Sec. 5.6 and both table footnotes. Statistical language is also disciplined: 'An interval crossing zero is not evidence of statistical equivalence' appears in the caption, in Sec. 5.4, and in the abstract.

The internal arithmetic of the audit apparatus is exactly self-consistent where it can be checked from the PDF alone: 209,920 = 20,992 x 10, 635,520 = 20,992 x 30 + 192 x 30, 96 = 8 x 3 x 4, 144 = 8 x 3 x 6, 12,960 = 8 x 3 x 540, 3,840 = 8 x 480, 540 = (1 + 8) x 60, 480 = 8 x 60. Nothing in the counts is inconsistent with itself.

Related-work positioning is honest about non-commensurability. Table 16's caption states that the cited systems' numbers 'show the scale and evaluation breadth of related systems, not a cross-paper leaderboard' and that 'the absence of a common score must not be read as a negative result'; Table 11 explicitly credits CoMem with the split-replay primitive.
questions: Is a research artifact submitted with this paper? The Reproducibility Statement and Appendix I Table 27 give ~30 relative paths 'rooted at the accompanying research package' plus internal registry entry IDs (E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A, E-R40-PRIMARY-COMPILED-DISPATCH-V11-A, ...), but the PDF contains no anonymous repository URL, no supplementary-material reference, and no availability statement. Where does a reviewer obtain the package that Appendix A says replays in ~100 s on a laptop?

Where is the implementation of the Q-CoMem quantizer, Write, and Read? method_provenance.tsv has 83 entries and none of them names a source file for Eq. 3, the group-of-64 packing, the Q4/Q4/Q8 assignment, the per-layer bit search, the dequantize-and-fork Read path, the LongBench F1 computation, or the paired bootstrap. The only entry touching the deployment table (M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION) points at scripts/generate_h20_deployment_table.py, which formats an already-frozen summary.

What decoding rule was used for the 60-item cohort in Table 1? 'greedy decoding' is stated only for the eight-item execution (Sec. 5.1 latency paragraph, Table 2, Tables 18 and 19). If Table 1 used sampling, the F1 values and the paired bootstrap intervals mean something different.

In Table 2, over what population is each 'median' taken - 8 items, 3 repeats, or all 24 measurements, and is it a median of per-item medians? No dispersion is reported for any timing value. Relatedly, how is 'generated-token throughput' defined? The three timing columns reconcile only under tok/s = n / (TTFT + n x TPOT), which implies n ~ 7.5-8.0 generated tokens per item against a stated 32-token cap. What were the actual generated lengths?

Does the 'no-cache dense recompute' arm retain a KV cache during decoding? Its TTFT (0.649 s) and TPOT (648.75 ms) are equal to within 0.04%, which is what one would see if the full prefix is re-run at every decode step.

Why do Table 1 and Table 2 report 136.235 vs 140.34 MiB/doc for full-prefix Q16, and 9.661 vs 10.01 MiB/doc for the same frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy? Table 2's eight items are a strict subset of Table 1's sixty, so both accountings can be computed on the same eight items. What is the measured difference?

What are the retained tensor shapes? Without hidden size, KV head count, head dimension, and GDN convolution/recurrent state shapes, Eq. 2 cannot be instantiated and no Store number can be independently derived. Also, what is the 'Q16 projections' component of the per-layer policy, given that Eq. 2 has no projection term?

Sec. 5.5 says 'The stronger same-run hook wraps only the selected N = 8 ... witness', while Appendix A says 'The separate live-binding rerun binds a different frozen archive to eight scientifically valid rank shards'. Are the seven-target verdicts (Table 6), the target-5 receipts, and the V29 selected-cell counts from one execution or from three? Which numbers belong to which run?
Why do LongBench, Qasper, and 2WikiMultihopQA never appear in the reference list, and which release/commit of the 'official LongBench-v1 prompts' and F1 implementation was used?

Should Appendix A's 'QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116' be replaced with a neutral alias, as the paper already does for the HYPIC artifact ('the anonymous package assigns a neutral artifact alias', Table 27)?

issues.location: Reproducibility Statement (p.9); Appendix A (pp.12-13); Appendix I Table 27 (pp.29-31); Sec. 5.5 (pp.7-8)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's entire reproducibility apparatus resolves to a package that is never made available. Appendix I Table 27 gives ~30 relative paths 'rooted at the accompanying research package' (evidence/round_04_rr2_package/replay/run_replay.sh, evidence/qcomem_mixed_validation_60item_20260812d/, evidence/experiment_registry.json entries, ...). Nowhere in 31 pages is there an anonymous repository URL, a supplementary-material reference, or a sentence stating that the package is submitted: grep over the full text finds zero occurrences of 'supplementary', 'available', 'anonymized', 'github', 'zenodo', or any http artifact link. Consequently every quantitative statement in Sec. 5.5 and Appendix A is supported only by an assertion of having run something: 209,920 attention and 635,520 GDN call receipts; 96 configurations and 192 rebuilt cells; 288 fan-out comparisons; 144 / 12,960 / 3,840 / 24 selected-cell units; 96,660 relations and 1,080 receiver rows; 536 raw artifacts; a 1,367-node terminal tree; 44 clean rows and 44 rejected controls; 224 and 184 rejected negative controls; 272 sidecars totalling 140,199,936 bytes. I hold pdf_plus_repository access and was given only claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv - two index files authored by the same pipeline - so I could not verify a single one of these counts against an artifact.
issues.why_it_matters: Roughly 40% of the main-text results section and most of the 22-page appendix consist of counts that no third party can re-derive, check, or falsify. Under the ICLR reviewer guide's reproducibility criterion this is the difference between evidence and testimony. It also makes the paper's central methodological selling point - that ForkAudit provides storage evidence rather than output equality - itself unauditable, which is precisely the failure mode the method is designed to prevent.
issues.required_fix: Attach an anonymized artifact (or state the exact availability mechanism and timing) that at minimum contains: the primary replay package and its one-command run_replay.sh; the 60-item validation package with raw shards and the F1/bootstrap/Store recomputation; and the eight-item timing shards. Add a one-paragraph 'Artifact availability' block immediately after the Reproducibility Statement naming what is included, its size, its runtime, and what is intentionally excluded.
issues.verification_test: A reviewer downloads the artifact on a CPU-only host, runs the advertised one-command replay, and confirms that it terminates in the Appendix-A-reported ~100 s and reproduces at least: Table 1's six Store values and six F1 values, the four bootstrap intervals cited in the text, Table 2's six Store values, and the 54.5% allocator delta - each byte-identical to the manuscript.
issues.evidence_needed: An anonymized artifact archive or repository link, plus a manifest mapping each numbered claim in the paper to a file inside it.

issues.location: Sec. 4.1-4.3 (pp.4-5), Eq. 2 and Eq. 3; Sec. 5.1-5.2 (pp.5-6); method_provenance.tsv (all 83 rows)
issues.observed_evidence: method_provenance.tsv contains 83 entries, and not one provides code or configuration provenance for the method the paper is named after. There is no entry for the groupwise quantizer of Eq. 3, the group size of 64, the BF16 scale/bias metadata layout, the offline Write that packs the complete entry at split depth j, the online Read that dequantizes and forks, the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 state-type assignment, the per-layer bit search on the four-item calibration set, the LongBench F1 implementation, the paired 10,000-resample bootstrap, or the component-sum Store accounting used for Table 1. Keyword counts over the file: 'quantiz' 0, 'dequant' 0, 'residual' 0, 'bootstrap' 0, 'LongBench' 0, '60-item' 0. The two hits for 'Q4'/'Q8' are in M-MAC-CONTROL-DERIVATION, an unpooled Apple-M4 motivation table. The only row touching the deployment numbers, M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION, points at scripts/generate_h20_deployment_table.py with symbols 'main; sha256; require; format_mib' - a formatter that reads an already-frozen summary. Every other row maps to ForkAudit ownership code (qcomem_vllm_paged_kernel.py, qcomem_qwen35_native_cache.py, replay_rr2.py, ...), related-work transfer ports, or table generators. The asymmetry is total: the complementary audit component has exhaustive provenance and the named contribution has none.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's headline results - 14.10x smaller retained state at -0.39 F1 - are produced by code that the provenance artifact does not reference at all. A reader cannot confirm that Eq. 3 is what was executed, that the reported bit assignment matches the implementation, that Store was summed over the components Eq. 2 lists, or that F1 and the bootstrap follow the stated definitions. Method statements in Sec. 4.1-4.3 are therefore asserted, not backed. This inverts the paper's own thesis: it argues that output equality is insufficient because implementations can diverge silently from their described semantics, yet the described semantics of Q-CoMem itself are unbacked by any code reference.
issues.required_fix: Add method_provenance rows (source path, symbol, configuration) for at minimum: the quantize/dequantize kernel implementing Eq. 3; the Write path that enumerates and packs the Eq. 2 components; the Read path (dequantize, fork, lower-layer replay, merge at j, suffix); the policy definitions for frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, same-memory per-layer, and aggressive mixed; the Store accounting function used for Table 1; and the F1 and bootstrap routines. Ship the corresponding files in the artifact.
issues.verification_test: Open the named quantizer source and confirm that group size is 64, that scale = (u - m) / (2^b - 1) with clipped rounding to [0, 2^b - 1], and that scale/bias are stored in BF16; then run the named Store accounting function over one archived document entry and confirm it returns 9.660873 MiB for the frozen policy and 136.235352 MiB for full-prefix Q16.
issues.evidence_needed: Source files and symbol names for the Q-CoMem Write/Read/quantizer/policy/accounting/metric code, plus the config that pins split depth j = 7 and the bit vectors.

issues.location: Appendix I Table 27 final row ('Manuscript claim index -> evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv', p.31); claim_evidence_map.tsv manuscript_locations column (all rows)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper designates claim_evidence_map.tsv as its manuscript claim index, but that index does not resolve against the manuscript under review. The reviewed PDF has Sections 1-6 (4 ends at 4.4, 5 ends at 5.6) plus Appendices A-I. The index repeatedly cites structure that does not exist: 'Sec. 4.5 [label:sec:protocol]' (C-MUT-01, C-RR2-MUT-01), 'Sec. 7 Reproducibility Statement' (C-R23-A1-TERMINAL-IDENTITY-01), 'Appendix J artifact map' (C-R23-A1-TERMINAL-IDENTITY-01), 'Appendix B lattice' and 'Appendix E capacity cohort' (C-CROSSN; Appendix B is the Ethics Statement and Appendix E is the fault-row appendix), and 'Appendix F [label:app:invariants]' when the invariant map is Appendix E. Table references are equally stale: C-H20-DEPLOYMENT-01 points at 'Sec. 5.2 ... Table [label:tab:h20-deployment]' while the deployment numbers are Table 2 in Sec. 5.3 and Table 18 in Appendix G.1. Most sharply, C-R40-INDEPENDENT-LIVE-BINDING-V29-01 records its location as 'Pending successor-TeX integration and fresh review; absent from the current reviewed candidate' - yet its numbers are in the reviewed PDF: Sec. 5.5 reports '144 selected-owner-row checks, 8 x 3 x 540 = 12,960 full serializer/live-object rows, 8 x 480 = 3,840 direct clone edges, and 8 x 3 = 24 stable artifacts', Table 4 is titled 'Meaning of the V29 selected-cell evidence units', and Appendix A cites the 1,367-node final tree. Separately, the three claim rows carrying the paper's headline numbers (C-QCOMEM-60-*) have no manuscript location at all, only 'Integrated in R42 and independently claim-audited on 2026-09-02'.
issues.why_it_matters: The index is the mechanism by which the paper promises a third party can trace each claim to evidence ('Claims map to registered evidence identifiers', Reproducibility Statement). A stale index means the traceability guarantee is nominal. It also shows the claim ledger was not audited against this manuscript version, which weakens confidence in every other assertion of pre-registration and freezing that a reader cannot check.
issues.required_fix: Regenerate claim_evidence_map.tsv against the submitted PDF: every manuscript_locations field must name a section number, table number, and figure number that exist in this build, and every claim appearing in the PDF must have a row whose location is non-empty and correct. Add rows or locations for the three C-QCOMEM-60-* claims, and correct the V29 row, which is present in the PDF rather than absent.
issues.verification_test: Script the index: for each row, parse manuscript_locations, resolve each section/appendix/table/figure reference against the compiled PDF's structure, and assert zero unresolved references and zero rows whose location says 'absent from the current reviewed candidate' while the row's distinctive numbers appear in the PDF text.
issues.evidence_needed: A regenerated claim index built from the same LaTeX source as the submitted PDF, plus the resolver script output.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.6); Table 1 footnote (p.6); Table 2 footnote (p.7); Sec. 5.2 (p.6); Sec. 5.6 (p.9)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's headline estimand is measured two different ways whose divergence is disclosed but never quantified. Sec. 5.1: 'the 60-item panel sums the stored persistent components (packed residual data, scales, biases, and unique lower-cache tensor storage), whereas the eight-item execution measures the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry.' On the same model, stack, token cap, and split depth, full-prefix Q16 is 136.235 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 140.34 MiB/doc in Table 2 (a 3.0% gap), and the same frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy is 9.661 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 10.01 MiB/doc in Table 2 (a 3.6% gap). Crucially, Table 2's eight items are a declared strict subset of Table 1's sixty (indices 6-9 of each dataset, stated in Sec. 5.1 and in Table 2's title), so this is not a cohort-composition artifact that cannot be untangled - both accountings are computable on the same eight documents. The paper's response is only to refuse pooling; the two derived compression figures it then quotes side by side in Sec. 5.2 (14.10x from one denominator, 92.87%/93.06% from the other) are not on a common scale.
issues.why_it_matters: A capacity-first paper must have one auditable definition of retained bytes. Without a cross-walk, a reader cannot tell whether the 3% divergence is definitional (metadata, alignment, shared storage attributed differently) or empirical (different packing behaviour between the two executions), and cannot combine the tables even mentally. It also blocks any external comparison: the HYPIC 8.78x/20.39x ratios in Table 18 use the byte-range estimand, while the paper's headline 14.10x uses the component estimand.
issues.required_fix: Compute both accountings on the eight shared items and add a short reconciliation table (component sum, byte-range union, and their difference decomposed into alignment/padding/shared-storage/metadata terms) for at least full-prefix Q16, split Q16, and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8. Then state which estimand is canonical for the paper's headline number.
issues.verification_test: Run both accounting implementations over the archived retained entries for source indices 6-9 of each dataset and confirm the reported per-item values and their difference; the reconciliation must account for the full 136.235 vs 140.34 and 9.661 vs 10.01 gaps within stated rounding.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-item Store values for the eight shared documents under both accounting implementations, plus the source of each accounting function.

issues.location: Eq. 2 and Sec. 4.1 (p.4); Sec. 4.2 (p.4); Table 2 footnote (p.7); Table 18 footnote (p.24); Table 3 (p.14)
issues.observed_evidence: Two problems make Eq. 2 non-instantiable. First, the model geometry needed to evaluate it is never given: Table 3 states only 'Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; 10 attention + 30 GDN layers', and no hidden size, KV head count, head dimension, GDN convolution width, or recurrent state shape appears anywhere in the paper. A reader therefore cannot derive any term of S_QCoMem(D; j, b), cannot check that 136.235 -> 34.683 is consistent with removing all but one lower attention layer, and cannot predict Store for any other depth or model. Second, the per-layer policy retains a component that Eq. 2 does not contain: Sec. 4.2 says 'the reported per-layer policy uses a Q4 residual, Q16 projections, and active-layer widths [8, 8, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8]', and both Table 2's and Table 18's footnotes repeat 'Q4 residual, Q16 projections'. Eq. 2 has exactly three terms - residual, lower KV, lower convolution/recurrent state - and 'projections' is defined nowhere in the paper. That row's Store (9.74 MiB in Table 2, 9.395 MiB as 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1) therefore cannot be reconstructed from the paper's own decomposition. The naming also shifts between tables: the same policy is 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1, 'per-layer mixed' in Table 2, and 'CoMem per-layer mixed' in Table 18.
issues.why_it_matters: Eq. 2 is the paper's formal statement of what it contributes - counting the whole entry rather than the residual alone. If the equation cannot be evaluated for the reported model and does not cover the components an evaluated policy actually retains, then the central accounting claim is not independently checkable and the ablation rows are not reproducible. This is the analytical counterpart of issue R44-5-05: neither the empirical nor the analytical route to Store is open to a reader.
issues.required_fix: Add a small table giving, for the evaluated configuration, the per-component retained tensor shapes and byte counts at BF16 and under each policy, so that the six Store values in Table 1 follow arithmetically from Eq. 2. Either add the projection term to Eq. 2 with a definition, or remove 'Q16 projections' from the policy descriptions. Use one name per policy across all tables.
issues.verification_test: From the published shapes and bit assignments, recompute S_QCoMem for full-prefix Q16, split Q16, frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, per-layer mixed, and aggressive mixed, and confirm agreement with 136.235, 34.683, 9.661, 9.395, and 7.536 MiB/doc within the stated group/metadata overhead.
issues.evidence_needed: Retained tensor shape/dtype inventory for one document entry, and a definition of the 'projections' component.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Quality cohort' and 'Latency execution' (pp.5-6); Table 1 (p.6); Table 2 (p.7); Sec. 5.3 (pp.6-7)
issues.observed_evidence: Five specifications needed to re-run are missing. (a) The decoding rule for the 60-item cohort is never stated; 'greedy decoding' appears only in the latency paragraph, Table 2, and Tables 18-19, so Table 1's decoding is unspecified. (b) Table 2's footnote says 'Store and timing/throughput columns are medians' without naming the population: 8 items, 3 repeats, 24 measurements, or a median of per-item medians. No dispersion (range, IQR, or per-item values) is reported for any timing number, so the '2.5%' TPOT statement and the 0.163-vs-0.673 contrast carry no uncertainty. (c) 'generated-token throughput' is never defined. The three timing columns are mutually consistent only under tok/s = n / (TTFT + n x TPOT); solving that relation gives n = 7.90 for full-prefix Q16, 7.97-8.02 for the four Q-CoMem rows, and 7.50 for dense - i.e. about eight generated tokens per item against a stated cap of 32. The actual generated lengths, which fully determine the throughput column, are never reported. (d) The 'aggressive mixed' row of Table 1 (7.536 MiB/doc, 18.08x, -5.44 F1, 5/60 catastrophic) has no stated bit assignment anywhere in the paper, so that row cannot be reproduced at all. (e) How the 4,096-token input cap is applied - LongBench-style middle truncation, head truncation, or tail truncation - is not stated, and it changes both Store and F1.
issues.why_it_matters: These are exactly the parameters that decide whether a re-run lands on 54.24 or somewhere else. Item (c) matters most: throughput is the metric the abstract uses to characterise the cost of the method, and it is reported without a definition, without dispersion, and without the token counts that drive it. Item (d) makes a row that the paper uses to argue against aggressive quantization non-reproducible.
issues.required_fix: State the decoding rule for the 60-item cohort; define the aggregation population and estimator for every median in Table 2 and add ranges or per-item values; define generated-token throughput explicitly (numerator, denominator, whether prefill is included) and report mean/median generated tokens per row; give the aggressive policy's bit vector; and state the truncation rule for the 4,096-token cap.
issues.verification_test: Recompute Table 2's tok/s column from the published per-item generated-token counts and per-item wall times using the stated definition and confirm the printed values; independently, regenerate Table 1's aggressive-mixed row from the published bit vector and confirm 7.536 MiB/doc and F1 49.19.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-item timing and generated-token records for the eight-item execution, decoding and truncation configuration for both cohorts, and the aggressive policy specification.

issues.location: Eq. 1 and Sec. 3 (p.3); Sec. 5.2 (p.6); Sec. 5.5 'Allocator reduction' (p.8); Sec. 5.6 (p.9)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper motivates itself with Eq. 1, in which the controllable term is the sum of S(D) over the hot document set H, and argues that 'the retained term is the only one that grows with how many documents a deployment keeps warm'. No experiment ever varies |H|, measures how many documents fit, or measures peak device memory under the quantized policy. Sec. 5.6 states outright that 'reducing Store does not by itself prove lower peak VRAM or serving capacity', and the abstract disclaims lower total process memory. The single measurement that touches an allocator (Sec. 5.5: 4.901 -> 2.229 GiB at N = 32, 54.5%) comes from the ownership factorial, uses a third denominator, varies KV sharing rather than quantization (Table 15 shows 'Full-copy KV / Materialized GDN' vs 'Shared-doc KV / Materialized GDN'), and Sec. 5.6 states that the two reductions 'are not additive or interchangeable'. Sec. 5.6 further excludes continuous batching, QPS, admission, eviction, and scheduler effects. So the deployment budget the paper introduces to justify the work is never instantiated with the method the paper proposes.
issues.why_it_matters: Without a capacity measurement the contribution reduces to an improvement in a proxy that the paper itself declines to connect to any deployment consequence. The honest scoping is commendable but does not substitute for evidence; a reader cannot tell whether 14.10x smaller retained payload translates into more resident documents, because the Store estimand excludes allocator pools, active workspace, and process memory - the terms that typically dominate whether an extra document fits.
issues.required_fix: Add one resident-document sweep on the reported stack: hold the model and a fixed request shape constant, admit documents 1, 2, 4, 8, ... until failure under full-prefix Q16, split Q16, and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, and report the maximum resident document count and the peak allocator bytes as a function of |H|. This is the smallest experiment that connects Eq. 1 to the method and does not require new datasets or new baselines.
issues.verification_test: Report max resident documents per policy and a peak-memory-versus-|H| curve; confirm that the slope of retained bytes per document matches the Table 1 Store values and state the observed intercept (weights + workspace + runtime).
issues.evidence_needed: A capacity sweep with peak allocator and, ideally, process/NVML memory alongside the Store proxy.

issues.location: Table 2 dense row (p.7); Sec. 5.3 (pp.6-7); Table 1 caption catastrophic-regression rule (p.6); Table 18 footnote (p.24)
issues.observed_evidence: The 'no-cache dense recompute' arm is never operationally defined, and its reported numbers imply an unusual configuration. Table 2 gives dense TTFT = 0.649 s and TPOT = 648.75 ms - equal to within 0.04% - which is the signature of re-running the full prefix at every decode step rather than prefilling once and decoding from a KV cache. Sec. 5.3 quotes this as a result ('dense recomputation has 648.75 ms TPOT'). The paper's only characterisations are Sec. 3's 'stores no document state but repeatedly processes the prefix' and Table 18's footnote 'no-cache recompute uses a different document/query execution boundary', neither of which says what happens during decoding. The definition is load-bearing beyond the timing table: Table 1's caption defines the registered catastrophic-regression rule as 'per-item Delta-F1-versus-dense <= -50 point', so the dense arm is the reference for a reported 0/60, 1/60, and 5/60 failure count.
issues.why_it_matters: If dense decodes without a KV cache, its TPOT and throughput are not a meaningful endpoint - no deployment runs that way - and the ~477x TPOT gap and 1.36 tok/s figure overstate the contrast that the split-replay design is positioned against. Because the same arm defines the catastrophic-regression baseline, an unstated difference in its execution boundary also touches the quality claims.
issues.required_fix: Define the dense arm precisely: whether the document is re-prefilled per query or per token, whether a KV cache is retained during decoding, and what the 'different document/query execution boundary' consists of. If it recomputes per token, add a standard cached-prefill dense arm and report both.
issues.verification_test: Instrument the dense arm to count forward passes over the document per query; confirm the count is 1 for a cached-prefill implementation, and report TTFT, TPOT, and tok/s for that implementation next to the current row.
issues.evidence_needed: The dense-arm execution configuration and per-query forward-pass counts.

issues.observed_evidence: Sec. 5.5 presents results from at least three distinct executions as one continuous account. It opens with 'All seven targets have complete mandatory-trace coverage and satisfy the registered pass criterion for the fresh frozen primary rerun', then immediately reports the 209,920/635,520 target-5 receipts, which Appendix A attributes to a different run ('The fresh compiled-dispatch rerun binds a frozen source archive to a passing eight-rank formal aggregate'). The ownership paragraph then reports the 96-configuration factorial and the V29 selected-cell counts together, describing the latter as 'The stronger same-run hook' - while Appendix A says 'The separate live-binding rerun binds a different frozen archive to eight scientifically valid rank shards and a terminally complete formal tree'. The main text never tells the reader that the seven-target verdict, the target-5 dispatch receipts, and the selected-cell live binding come from separate executions, and Table 6 does not state which execution it summarises. The verdict vocabulary is also undefined: 'scientifically valid', 'terminally complete', and 'operationally invalid' (Appendix E) are load-bearing labels with no definition in the paper.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader of the 9-page main text will reasonably conclude that one frozen run produced the complete seven-target pass, the call-provenance receipts, and the strongest ownership binding. It did not. For an audit contribution whose entire value proposition is that receipts must be bound to a specific frozen execution, conflating three executions in the narrative undercuts the methodology being advocated, and it makes the results impossible to attribute or re-run selectively.
issues.required_fix: Give each execution a short identifier (e.g. PRIMARY-A, DISPATCH-B, LIVEBIND-C), tag every number in Sec. 5.5 and Table 6 with its execution, state which execution the seven-target verdict belongs to, and replace 'same-run' with wording that matches Appendix A. Define 'scientifically valid', 'terminally complete', and 'operationally invalid' at first use.
issues.verification_test: Cross-check every count in Sec. 5.5 against Appendix A and Table 5, and confirm that each is attributed to exactly one named execution with no number appearing under two different runs.
issues.evidence_needed: An execution-to-result attribution table for the primary factorial, the dispatch rerun, and the live-binding rerun.

issues.location: Abstract (p.1); Sec. 5.5 'Falsification beyond output equality' (p.8); Table 14 caption (p.21); Appendix H (p.28)
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract states that 'a fail-closed ownership audit exposes a historical alias invisible to output equality', and Sec. 5.5 reports only that 'output and terminal request state remain exact in 8/8 cells despite persistent-base corruption'. The qualification that a conventional check also catches the defect appears twice, both outside the main text: Table 14's caption says 'Base inv.' is 'within-path persistent-base immutability, retained as a conventional state-invariant catch', and Appendix H states 'Output and terminal-state differentials miss the alias, while a persistent-base content invariant catches it; ForkAudit contributes authenticated transition-time owner/layer/family localization rather than exclusive detection over all conventional testing.' The claim map goes further in an internal-only row (C-R40-BASELINE-DETECTOR-MATRIX-01): a 'generous frozen conventional suite flagged 21/22'.
issues.why_it_matters: Nothing in the abstract or Sec. 5.5 is false, but a reader of the 9-page main text gets the stronger reading that the audit was necessary to find the alias, when the paper's own appendix says a conventional persistent-base content invariant suffices for detection and that the audit's incremental value is localization. The correction sits 20 pages later.
issues.required_fix: Add one clause to Sec. 5.5 (and, if space allows, to the abstract): a conventional persistent-base content invariant also detects this defect; ForkAudit's incremental contribution is authenticated transition-time owner/layer/family localization, not exclusive detection.
issues.verification_test: Confirm that the main text's statement of the historical-alias result is logically identical to Appendix H's, with no qualification present only in the appendix.
issues.evidence_needed: None; this is a wording change.

issues.observed_evidence: The paper's only quality benchmark and both of its datasets are used without citation. 'Official LongBench-v1 prompts', 'LongBench answer F1', and the '0-100 LongBench scale' appear throughout Sec. 5.1, Sec. 5.4, and five table captions, and Qasper and 2WikiMQA appear in every quality table, but the reference list (Chang, Chen, Fu, Gao, Gim, Juravsky, Kwon, Lenz, Li, Liu x3, Pan, Pham, Qwen x2, Rae, Srivatsa, Wang, Xiao, Yang, Ye, Zheng, Zuo) contains no LongBench, Qasper, or 2WikiMultihopQA entry. PG-19 is cited (Rae et al., 2020) and every prior system is cited, so the omission is specific to the datasets that produce the headline quality numbers. No release, revision, or prompt-file version is given for LongBench-v1 either.
issues.why_it_matters: Credit aside, this is a reproducibility gap: 'official LongBench-v1 prompts' and the F1 implementation are version-sensitive, and 'source indices 6-35' is only meaningful relative to a specific dataset release and ordering.
issues.required_fix: Cite LongBench, Qasper, and 2WikiMultihopQA, and pin the dataset release/revision plus the F1 implementation (repository and commit) used for the reported scores.
issues.verification_test: Confirm the reference list contains all three, and that a third party can load the pinned release and reproduce the item ordering implied by 'source indices 4-5' (calibration) and '6-35' (validation).

issues.observed_evidence: Appendix A states 'The 60-item quality package preserves 66 authoritative mirrored files from QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116, including 48 configuration-by-rank shards.' This is an internal compute-platform job and trial identifier. It conveys nothing verifiable to a reader with the paper, and it is the kind of internal-system identifier that can narrow authorship under double-blind review. The paper elsewhere shows it knows how to handle this: Table 27's HYPIC row notes that 'the anonymous package assigns a neutral artifact alias'.
issues.why_it_matters: It is simultaneously an anonymity risk and a piece of pseudo-provenance: a reader cannot resolve a job ID on a private cluster, so the sentence adds the appearance of traceability without the substance.
issues.required_fix: Replace the job/trial identifier with a neutral archive alias plus the package SHA-256 that a reviewer can actually check against the supplied artifact.
issues.verification_test: Grep the camera-ready for internal job, trial, cluster, and ticket identifiers; confirm each is replaced by a content hash or neutral alias.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Quality cohort' (p.5); Table 1 caption (p.6); Sec. 5.6 (pp.8-9); Appendix A (p.12); Appendix H (p.28)
issues.observed_evidence: Sec. 5.1 asserts an exact stack for the headline cohort - 'Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.14.1, and eight H20-3e GPUs' - for a run that, per Sec. 5.6 and Appendix A, 'retained neither a pre-run full-source ledger nor a full model-weight ledger'. The claim map is candid that 'exact full-weight identity' is a rejected expansion for this cohort (C-UNSUPPORTED-QCOMEM-60-EXPANSION). The disclosure is present and correct in Sec. 5.6, Appendix A, Appendix H, and Table 5, but it is not attached to Sec. 5.1 or Table 1, which is where the stack and model identity are asserted as fact and where a reader forms their impression of the headline numbers. Separately, the split depth j = 7 used by every reported cohort appears only inside Figure 2 and never in the prose of Sec. 4 or Sec. 5.
issues.why_it_matters: For a paper whose thesis is that provenance must be bound to the artifact rather than asserted, the one cohort carrying the headline result asserts its model and stack without a ledger, and does so three pages before the caveat. Placing the caveat next to the assertion costs one sentence and removes any chance of a misread. The missing prose statement of j = 7 means the single most important method hyperparameter is figure-only.
issues.required_fix: Add a clause to Sec. 5.1's quality-cohort paragraph or Table 1's caption noting that this cohort's source and model-weight identity are not ledgered and that the stack is reported as recorded rather than attested. State the split depth j = 7 in the prose of Sec. 4.1 or 5.1.
issues.verification_test: Confirm that every location asserting the 60-item cohort's stack carries the ledger caveat within the same paragraph or caption, and that j = 7 appears in body text.
issues.evidence_needed: None; this is a placement change.

issues.observed_evidence: The same systems on overlapping items score F1 ~54 in Table 1 and ~39 in Table 2 (frozen Q4/Q4/Q8: 54.24 vs 39.01; full-prefix Q16: 54.68 vs 39.14). Table 2's eight items are a declared subset of Table 1's sixty. The paper says only that the two panels use a 'separate protocol' and 'are not pooled'. The likely cause is visible but never stated: Table 1 allows Qasper up to 128 generated tokens while the eight-item execution caps all items at 32, and n = 8 versus n = 60 changes the dataset mix. Neither explanation is given, and no per-item values are reported for either panel.
issues.why_it_matters: A ~15-point F1 gap between two tables describing the same method on overlapping items invites the reader to suspect one of them is wrong. One sentence of explanation would remove the doubt, and per-item values would let a reader verify the subset relationship directly.
issues.required_fix: State explicitly why the F1 levels differ between the panels (generation cap, item count, dataset mix), and report the Table 1 F1 restricted to the eight shared items alongside the Table 2 values.
issues.verification_test: Recompute Table 1's mean F1 over source indices 6-9 of each dataset under the Table 2 generation cap and confirm it lands at the Table 2 values within the stated protocol difference.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-item F1 for both cohorts on the eight shared documents.

ethics_concerns: No ethics flag. Appendix B is an adequate ethics statement: no human-subject data, public PG-19 text plus public QA benchmarks, and an honest note that efficiency gains can lower cost while increasing the scale of model use. No safety, bias, privacy, or dual-use concern arises from the contribution. Two non-ethics integrity notes are recorded as issues instead: the internal 'QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116' identifier in Appendix A is a mild double-blind identifiability risk (R44-5-13), and the paper carries no LLM-use disclosure, which may simply mean there was no significant LLM use but is worth confirming against the ICLR 2026 submission requirement.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM reviewer (Claude, Opus 5) operating under the R44-REV-5 reproducibility_provenance role with pdf_plus_repository access restricted to the frozen snapshot 0a8cb47a. The model performed all work: it extracted the 31-page PDF with pdftotext -layout, inspected pages 4, 6, and 13 as rendered images, parsed claim_evidence_map.tsv (66 claim rows) and method_provenance.tsv (83 method rows), cross-checked every numeric cell of Tables 1 and 2 against those files, verified the paper's internal arithmetic (compression ratios, percentage reductions, call-count factorizations, selected-cell unit products, allocator deltas), and inverted the Table 2 timing relations to recover the implied generated-token counts. No human verified the findings independently. No text from the manuscript or the artifact files was treated as an instruction to the reviewer.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: An anonymized artifact whose one-command replay regenerates Table 1's Store and F1 values, the four quoted bootstrap intervals, Table 2's Store values, and the 54.5% allocator delta byte-for-byte on a CPU-only host, exactly as Appendix A promises. This alone would convert roughly half the paper from testimony to evidence and would move me to 6.

method_provenance rows and shipped source for the Q-CoMem quantizer (Eq. 3), the Write/Read paths, the three policy definitions, the Store accounting function, and the F1/bootstrap routines - so that the named contribution has at least the provenance the audit component already has.

A resident-document capacity sweep on the reported stack showing maximum resident documents and peak allocator bytes versus |H| under full-prefix Q16 and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8. Connecting the 14.10x proxy to Eq. 1's budget would raise contribution from 2 to 3 and, combined with the artifact, would support 8.

A denominator cross-walk computing both Store accountings on the eight shared items, decomposing the 136.235-vs-140.34 and 9.661-vs-10.01 gaps into alignment, padding, shared-storage, and metadata terms, plus a retained-tensor shape table that makes Eq. 2 evaluable in closed form.

A fresh, source-frozen regeneration of the quality cohort (even at reduced size, e.g. the same 60 items on a ledgered run) that reproduces the frozen policy's Store and F1 within the reported bootstrap interval, removing the paper's single largest provenance asymmetry.

Full timing specification for Table 2: definition of generated-token throughput, the aggregation population for each median, per-item dispersion, and the actual generated-token counts (which my inversion suggests are ~8, not the stated 32 cap).
A second model family or a second hardware family for the capacity-quality result, even at small scale, to show the 14.10x is not specific to this one Qwen3.5 geometry and split depth.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Discovery that the 'accompanying research package' does not exist in a form a third party can run, or that the one-command replay does not reproduce the manuscript values - which would make Sec. 5.5 and Appendix A unsupported rather than merely unverifiable, and would justify 2.
Confirmation that the Q-CoMem quantizer/Write/Read code cannot be produced, i.e. that the method described in Sec. 4.1-4.3 is not the code that generated Tables 1 and 2.

Evidence that the 60-item archival run's model or stack differs from what Sec. 5.1 states - a live possibility precisely because no source or model-weight ledger was kept, and one that the claim map already flags by rejecting 'exact full-weight identity' for that cohort.

Confirmation that the 'no-cache dense recompute' arm decodes without a KV cache, which would make the 648.75 ms TPOT and 1.36 tok/s a strawman and would also raise questions about the dense-referenced catastrophic-regression counts in Table 1.

A recomputation showing that the two Store accountings differ by substantially more than 3% on the shared items, or that the 14.10x shrinks materially under the byte-range estimand the paper uses for its external HYPIC comparison.

Any indication that the 60-item and eight-item panels share more than the stated indices-6-9 overlap in a way that makes the eight-item execution a partial re-report of the same measurements rather than a separate execution.
review_limitations: Access was limited to the frozen snapshot: the manuscript PDF, review-rubric.md, claim_evidence_map.tsv, and method_provenance.tsv. The 'accompanying research package' referenced throughout Appendix I was not provided, so I could not execute any replay, open any source file, or confirm the existence of any evidence/ path. Every provenance finding is therefore a statement about what the submission makes checkable, not a claim that the underlying work was not done.

The two TSVs are index files produced by the same pipeline as the manuscript. They can corroborate that a printed value matches a recorded value, but they are not independent evidence, and I treated agreement between them and the PDF as consistency rather than verification.
I did not read the LaTeX source, prior reviews, revision notes, decision logs, or any author state file, per the access boundary.

The implied generated-token counts (~7.5-8.0) in issue R44-5-07 were obtained by inverting tok/s = n / (TTFT + n x TPOT) on medians. Medians do not commute with that relation, so the derived counts are indicative rather than exact; the underlying point - that the throughput definition and the actual token counts are unstated - does not depend on the inversion.

I am not able to verify the existence or geometry of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B or H20-3e independently, so I took the model, hardware, and library versions as reported and did not attempt to audit whether the stated stack is internally plausible beyond the checks noted above.
My assessment of novelty relative to CoMem (Liu et al., 2026a;b) rests on the paper's own description of that work; I did not have access to those papers.
